summary: Wooden live-in tower built 1944 at Tahuya in Mason County, abandoned 1957 and later removed. Site lies inside Tahuya State Forest; no source describes its remains today.

facts.status_note: Abandoned in 1957 and later removed; firelookout.com marks it gone

access.note: Site lies inside Tahuya State Forest, which the DNR describes as open to public trail use; Willhite gives road directions with a gate on Elfendahl Pass Road; no source says the site is closed

visit.trail_note: No tower remains to climb according to the sources read; Willhite's directions end at a pullout and gate on Elfendahl Pass Road, and he says an easy road walk of about a half mile reaches the site (the start point of that walk is not stated)

events.note: Wooden live-in tower built on the site; the 1944 Division of Forestry annual report records one new lookout tower erected at Tahuya
Aircraft Warning Service station recorded on May 1, 1944 on private land; AWS funding paid for a 14 x 32 cabin; the State of Washington retained the site when the service ended
Abandoned in 1957 per the register and firelookout.com; Willhite says abandoned by 1957
Firefinder from the lookout photographed at a DNR facility
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register on February 11, 2020

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Weebly's 1944 AWS listing says the station was on private land. Willhite places the site inside the Tahuya State Forest today. The sources do not say when the land came under state ownership.

The register and firelookout.com describe a wooden live-in tower; the 1944 AWS note describes a 14 x 32 cabin funded by AWS. The sources do not say whether these are the same structure, so the story reports them separately.

sources.title: Green Mountain and Tahuya State Forest

notes_for_editor: Four pages agree on the 1944 build and 1957 abandonment; the removal date is not given anywhere read. The register's 2020 registration date matches the brief. The 1944 annual report is quoted second-hand through the weebly page. The DNR page is a general state forest page; it shows two unrelated recreation alerts and does not mention the lookout, so public access is inferred from the forest's public trail use and no closure was found. Whether the AWS 14 x 32 cabin and the live-in tower are one structure is not stated. No photo URLs were read, so none were added; the firefinder photo credited to Willhite has no URL here. Two web searches added the DNR page and no source on the site today. Fact-check 2026-10-09: 'mostly gone' is now 'little view left', following Willhite's wording; the word 'nearby' was dropped from the DNR-cut sentence; Willhite does not say where the half-mile walk starts.
